CONFIG.SOLUTION_MANAGE_PRESCRIPTIONS_DESC: Here you can manage your prescriptions and generate QR codes to share with pharmacists.
CONFIG.SOLUTION_MANAGE_PRESCRIPTIONS_HTML:
Objective: register, view and generate QR Codes of prescriptions to present to the pharmacist or caregiver.

  1. On Home, tap the 'Manage prescriptions and QR Codes' card.
  2. On the prescriptions screen: tap 'Add Prescription' (or +).
  3. Fill in the requested fields: patient name, doctor's prescription, issue date, validity and notes.
  4. Attach the prescription photo: tap 'Add image' → choose a photo from gallery or use the camera.
  5. Tap Save / Confirm. The prescription will appear in the list.
  6. To generate a QR Code: select the desired prescription → tap 'Generate QR Code'.
  7. The app will show the QR; tap Share to send via WhatsApp/Email or Print if available.
  8. To edit or delete: select the prescription → Edit to change information or Delete to remove (confirm deletion).

Security tip: check the validity and allow only authorized caregivers to access — use the Share feature with permission.
CONFIG.SOLUTION_MEDICATION_REMINDERS_DESC: Set automatic reminders so you don't forget to take your medications on time.
CONFIG.SOLUTION_MEDICATION_REMINDERS_HTML:
Objective: create schedule alerts, repetition and track administrations.

  1. On Home, tap the 'Medication Reminders & Schedules' card.
  2. Tap 'Add Reminder' or the '+' button.
  3. Fill in: Medication name; Dosage (e.g., 500 mg); Form (tablet, syrup, injection); Times (e.g., 08:00, 12:00, 20:00); Frequency (daily, specific days); Duration (until date X or for N days).
  4. Enable sound/push and, if available, choose whether the reminder repeats on weekends.
  5. Save. The reminder will appear in the list with status (Active/Paused).
  6. When time comes: the app will show a notification with 'Mark as Taken' or 'Remind Later' buttons.
  7. History: tap the reminder → view history of taken doses and missed ones.
  8. Settings: go to Settings → Medication Alerts to configure volume, vibration and silent mode.

Tip for seniors: use large text (Settings → Accessibility → Text Size) and a loud alert sound.
CONFIG.SOLUTION_MEDICATION_INFO_DESC: View detailed medication information, side effects, and interactions.
CONFIG.SOLUTION_MEDICATION_INFO_HTML:
Objective: consult description, side effects, contraindications and usage instructions.

  1. On Home, tap the 'Medication Information' card.
  2. Use the search box to type the medication name.
  3. In the result list, tap the desired medication to open its record.
  4. The record includes: Indications; Dosage instructions; Side effects; Interactions with other medications; Precautions and contraindications; Doctor's notes (when linked to a prescription).
  5. To save for quick access: tap 'Favorite'.
  6. If technical doubt exists: tap 'Ask the Specialist' (or Specific Doubts — routes to support/FAQ channel).
  7. Tip: enable reading mode (eye icon) to simplify text and enlarge font.
CONFIG.SOLUTION_SPECIFIC_DOUBTS_DESC: Section with information and frequently asked questions tailored for older adults.
CONFIG.SOLUTION_SPECIFIC_DOUBTS_HTML:
Objective: dedicated area with simple language, support and FAQs tailored for seniors.

  1. On Home, tap the 'Specific Doubts for Seniors' card.
  2. The screen will open sections like: How to store medicines, How to take correctly, Warning signs, Accessibility.
  3. Browse quick topics (buttons/accordion). Tap to open the simple-language explanation.
  4. Questions & Answers (FAQ): tap an item to see the detailed answer and practical examples.
  5. Talk to an agent: tap 'Help & Support' → choose Chat, Call (if available) or Schedule a call with caregivers/administrator.
  6. Extra resources: short videos (play icon) about safe medication administration and printable checklists.
  7. Usability tip: enable Elder Mode in settings for larger buttons, high contrast and read-aloud (if available).
  8. Common steps to edit/add (prototype buttons).

PRIVACY.TITLE: Privacy Policy
PRIVACY.PRIVACY_HTML:
MedTime values your privacy and protects your personal data in accordance with applicable data protection laws.

What we collect:

- Data you provide: name, email, phone, medications, history and health conditions.

- App usage data: QR Code scans, usage times, device type and visited pages.

How we use it:

- To send alerts and record medication usage.

- To display medication information, such as leaflets.

- To improve the platform with anonymous data.

- To ensure the security of the service.

Security and sharing:

Your data is stored securely and only shared with partners essential to provide the service. We do not sell your data.

Your rights:

You can access, correct or delete your data and manage permissions at any time. This policy may be updated. You will be informed in the app or site if important changes occur.

If you have questions about the Privacy Policy, contact us

Email: suporte@medtime.com

TERMS.TITLE: Terms of Use
TERMS.TERMS_HTML:
At MedTime, we value your privacy and the security of your information. This policy explains clearly how we collect, use, process and protect your data when you use the app and the site.

What information do we collect?

Data you provide: Your name, email and phone number. Information about your medications (name, dosage, schedules, administration history). QR Code data: medication information read via QR Code.

How do we use your information?

Provide the MedTime service: To send medication alerts, record your administration history and display leaflets. Improve MedTime: We use anonymous and aggregated data to understand how the app is used. Communicate with you: To protect and send service or update notices.

If you have questions about the Privacy Policy, contact us

Email: suporte@medtime.com

LOGIN.FAQ_A1: MedTime was developed to help users manage their medical treatment more efficiently.
LOGIN.FAQ_Q2: Is the site responsive and works on different devices?
LOGIN.FAQ_A2: Yes. MedTime was designed with a responsive layout, which allows use on computers, tablets and mobile phones without loss of visual quality or functionality.
LOGIN.FAQ_Q3: How does the QR Code reading system work?
LOGIN.FAQ_A3: The user can scan a QR Code present on the medical prescription. The system interprets the data and schedules a series of alarms to remind the user to take medications at the correct times.
LOGIN.FAQ_A4: Anyone who needs to organize their medications can use MedTime, especially the elderly, caregivers, people with chronic diseases or any user who wants to improve their medication routine.
LOGIN.FAQ_A5: Yes. MedTime uses basic security practices, such as password encryption and login access control, ensuring that each user's data is protected.
LOGIN.FAQ_Q6: How can MedTime help in the user's daily life?
LOGIN.FAQ_A6: MedTime facilitates the organization of the medication routine, avoiding forgetfulness and dosing errors. With automatic reminders, quick reading of prescriptions via QR Code and a simple interface, it promotes greater safety and autonomy for the user in daily medical treatment.

DASHBOARD.FAQ_A1: A protein produced by the immune system to neutralize a pathogenic agent (virus, bacteria).
DASHBOARD.FAQ_Q2: What type of exercise is considered the most important for cardiovascular health?
DASHBOARD.FAQ_A2: Aerobic exercises (such as walking, running, swimming), which strengthen the heart and improve circulation.
DASHBOARD.FAQ_Q3: What is the main function of REM sleep (Rapid Eye Movement)?
DASHBOARD.FAQ_A3: It is the phase where most dreams occur and is crucial for memory processing and learning
DASHBOARD.FAQ_Q4: What percentage of total energy does the brain use that the body consumes?
DASHBOARD.FAQ_A4: Approximately 20% of energy and oxygen, even though it weighs only about 2% of total body weight.
DASHBOARD.FAQ_Q5: What condition is the main modifiable risk factor for heart disease, stroke and type 2 diabetes?
DASHBOARD.FAQ_Q6: What is the main difference between a virus and a bacterium?
DASHBOARD.FAQ_A6: Bacteria is a single-celled organism that can replicate itself, while a virus is a particle that needs to invade a host cell to replicate.

ABOUT.TITLE: Transform your treatment. With MedTime, technology cares for you, dose by dose.
ABOUT.KNOW_MEDTIME_TEXT: MedTime was born with the purpose of simplifying health management, transforming medication care into an easy and safe routine. We believe that technology can be a great ally for the well-being of everyone, especially our elderly. Our goal is to offer an accessible, intuitive and reliable platform that helps users control schedules, dosages and important information about their medications. With MedTime, we seek to promote more autonomy, security and quality of life, both for patients and for caregivers and family members. Taking care of health has never been so easy, intelligent and humane.
ABOUT.OUR_OBJECTIVE_TEXT: Our goal? More than controlling schedules: we want to democratize access to medical information, ensure safety in the use of medications and offer autonomy so that each person can take care of their own health with confidence. We believe that everyone deserves to have control over their treatments, understand what they are taking and why, and feel supported at each stage of care. MedTime was designed to go beyond technology is about empathy, accessibility and inclusion. We want to transform the way people relate to their health, making care simpler, smarter and closer to each user's reality.
ABOUT.BEHIND_MEDTIME_TEXT: MedTime is the result of a final study project, dedicated, developed by Iasmin de Arruda, Giovana Miguel and Isabella Romão. We are three students passionate about technology, health and innovation, united by the purpose of creating solutions that positively impact people's lives. Throughout the technical course in Systems Development, we faced real challenges, studied deeply about digital accessibility and understood the importance of creating an application that was, above all, useful, practical and human. Every line of code was thought through carefully, every screen planned with empathy. More than an academic project, MedTime is a reflection of our commitment to the future of digital health and the well-being of all.

CURIOSITIES.TITLE: Curiosity of the Day
CURIOSITIES.Q1_TITLE: Did you know that hydration is fundamental for the absorption of medications?
CURIOSITIES.Q1_TEXT: Water helps dissolve and transport the active ingredients of medicines through the body, facilitating their absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Additionally, adequate hydration contributes to the proper functioning of the kidneys, an organ essential in the metabolism and excretion of medications. Therefore, drinking water regularly not only improves overall health, but also enhances the effect of drug treatments.
CURIOSITIES.Q2_TITLE: Does sleeping well strengthen the immune system?
CURIOSITIES.Q2_TEXT: During sleep, especially in the deeper phases, the body produces cytokines proteins that help fight infections, inflammation and stress. Sleep deprivation reduces the production of these substances, weakening the immune response. People who sleep less than 6 hours a night are at higher risk of getting sick after exposure to viruses, such as the flu.
